notes: Check batch 2026-10-23-check-2: four skill runs (haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), no Opus, so the opus tier is unavailable in per_rule. All have rc 0, head 4215aa3, uncommitted true and skill_hash 508dfa8c8eacffabbd3539ab1bc01804bb7377edf055d64760f12d775cf1e9bd, which equals evals/tools/common.py folder_hash of the working tree's idiomatic-elixir/. Each model_id matches its tier; the only other model name in the transcripts is claude-opus-5-5 once per transcript, the tool-definition model option noted in 2026-10-23-check. Each transcript contains the new rule's heading text, so the runs read the working-tree SKILL.md. Reads: haiku-1 SKILL.md, processes.md, ecto-phoenix.md and library-design.md; the other three SKILL.md, processes.md and ecto-phoenix.md. Haiku-2 read SKILL.md with cat in Bash and the two reference files with Read; the others used Read for all. Expected reads (processes.md) is met in all four.

Changed rules: git diff d04061d -- idiomatic-elixir/ (working tree) adds one rule, "Keep a `->` clause on one line only when its pattern and body are each one plain term", and changes nothing else. The ten other listed rules are graded to the standard of sweeps/2026-10-23/grades/rate-limiter-skill.json and rate-limiter-baseline.json. The new rule is graded against its text; the sentences that decide the verdicts are "A clause of `case`, `cond`, `with ... else`, `fn` or `receive` stays on one line when the pattern is one plain term (an atom, a tuple or map one level deep, a variable) and the body is one call or one literal." and "A pattern that holds a binary, a guard or nesting, or a body that holds a nested call or a string built with `#{}`, goes on the line after the `->`."

New rule, counts: 3 of 4 runs violate it (haiku-1, sonnet-1, sonnet-2); 4 of 4 exercise it (every run has at least one case in code). Clauses that decide a verdict. haiku-1 line 113: |> Map.new(fn {user_id, timestamps} -> {user_id, in_window(timestamps, now)} end) (body is a tuple holding a call); haiku-1 line 184: case Enum.find(users, fn {_user_id, limit} -> not valid_limit?(limit) end) do (body is not/1 wrapping a call). sonnet-1 line 187: {:ok, [term]} -> {:ok, term} (pattern nests a list in a tuple); sonnet-1 line 188: {:ok, terms} -> {:error, {:expected_one_term, length(terms)}} (body holds the nested call length/1). sonnet-2 line 164: [{_key, limit}] -> limit (pattern nests a tuple in a list). Clean deciding clauses: haiku-2's only code case (lines 92-110) is broken, with {:error, reason} -> on line 108 and its body on line 109 after a blank line; sonnet-2 lines 110-115 (count when count <= limit -> with the body on the next line, blank line, count -> broken too) follow the guard sentence and the keep-the-layout sentence; one-line clauses kept as plain: haiku-1 line 114 fn {_user_id, timestamps} -> timestamps == [] end (one operator call on plain terms), haiku-1 lines 156-157 and 185-186, sonnet-1 lines 189 and 194, sonnet-2 line 133 fn {user, limit} -> :ets.insert(name, {{:limit, user}, limit}) end (one call; its nested tuple is a literal, not a call), sonnet-2 line 165. A nested tuple literal as a body with no call in it ({:error, {:unreadable_config, config_path, reason}}, haiku-1 line 157) is read as one literal and kept.

New rule, closest calls. (1) sonnet-2 line 164 and sonnet-1 line 187 turn on reading a list that wraps a tuple or variable as nesting; the rule names only tuples and maps one level deep as plain, so both count. Under a reading that treats the ETS lookup result [{_key, limit}] as plain, sonnet-2 is clean and the count is 2 of 4; sonnet-1 still violates through line 188. (2) haiku-1 line 184 turns on counting not/1 as a call, so not valid_limit?(limit) holds a nested call; line 113 decides haiku-1 without it. (3) Clauses inside @moduledoc examples are not counted, following the standard that layout inside a docstring is not graded (2026-10-23: "moduledoc tuples the author wrapped inside the docstring are not counted"), because mix format does not touch them. Counting them changes no verdict: the one moduledoc clause that would break the rule is sonnet-2 line 59, {:error, {:rate_limited, retry_after_ms}} -> {:snooze, div(retry_after_ms, 1000) + 1}, in a run already violated; haiku-2 lines 45-46 and sonnet-1 lines 75-76 are plain. Every broken case in the four files keeps all its clauses broken with blank lines between them, so the case file's 'once one clause breaks, every clause does' part is met in all four.

Standard carried over: an if on one boolean condition, including one joined with and, is clean (haiku-2 line 142, sonnet-1 line 194); a two-step with that calls File.read/1 and JSON.decode/1 directly with no else is clean (haiku-2 lines 135-136, as 2026-10-22-d haiku-2); a two-step with whose body returns a third fallible call is not counted (haiku-1 line 150); a run with no with and only raising boot-time calls is not exercised under the with rule (sonnet-2); all counts behind GenServer.call violate Pick the abstraction and Use ETS (haiku-1, as 2026-10-23 haiku-1); reading the limits file in init/1 is a missed case check but decides no verdict; key, term, decoded and similar names are not counted under Naming; moduledoc placeholder comments (sonnet-1 line 30 # lib/my_app/application.ex, sonnet-2 line 43 # ... do the work) are not counted under Comments; missing doctests are not counted, and haiku-2's start_link/1 having @spec but no @doc (lines 82-83) is likewise not counted, as earlier grades did not grade absent documentation elements.

Judgment calls new to this batch. Sonnet-1 lines 180-182 (with {:ok, term} <- consult(path) do / parse_limits(term) / end) is a one-step with whose body calls a second fallible function, so the with rule is violated under "A `with` has at least two `<-` steps; one step is a `case`." and "When the body of a one-step `with` calls another function that can fail, that call is the second step". Sonnet-2 lines 109-116 branch on count with a guard (count when count <= limit ->) rather than if; the count is used in both branches, and this is not the case ... true -> ... false -> form the Branch rule forbids, so Branch stays clean.

Designs. Haiku-1 went back to a single GenServer, as the 2026-10-23 haiku-1 did: check/2 is GenServer.call(server, {:check, user_id}) and handle_call/3 keeps per-user timestamp lists in state, so Pick the abstraction and Use ETS are violated. Haiku-2, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 keep one ETS row per admitted request in a public ordered_set table owned by a GenServer; the caller inserts its row, counts, and deletes the row when over; a handle_info/2 sweep deletes expired rows. Limits live in :persistent_term (haiku-2, sonnet-1) or as rows in the same table (sonnet-2). Sonnet-1 reads an Erlang-term file with :file.consult/1; sonnet-2 reads JSON with File.read!/JSON.decode! in init/1 and raises on bad limits. Every run reads its limits file inside init/1.

Verification, in scratch copies under grader-2026-10-23-check-2-rate-limiter. All four pass mix format --check-formatted and compile with elixirc --warnings-as-errors (Elixir 1.20.3); the only lines over 98 characters are sonnet-1 lines 22 (moduledoc) and 194 and sonnet-2 line 28 (moduledoc). In every run a 50-task concurrent burst admitted exactly 2 for a user at the default limit of 2 and 5 for user 42, configured at 5; a second instance under name: :other admitted 2 of 50; an injected 61-second-old entry was removed by one :sweep message and the live entries kept.

Violations among the listed rules: haiku-1 three (the new -> rule, Pick the abstraction, Use ETS); sonnet-1 two (the new -> rule, with); sonnet-2 one (the new -> rule); haiku-2 none. No rule outside the list was seen broken.
